facts.text: Quitman became the county seat of newly formed Brooks County in 1858, was incorporated as a town in 1859, and grew into a city by 1904.
The town’s name honors John A., a local figure whose legacy lives on in Quitman’s streets and history.
Quitman’s historic district earned a spot on the National Register of Historic Places, preserving its 19th‑century architecture.
The Quitman Brooks County Museum, housed in a downtown historic building, showcases clothing, furniture, photographs, and documents from the 19th and 20th centuries.
James Pierpont, the composer of “Jingle Bells,” called Quitman home, adding a musical note to the town’s heritage.
Every October, the museum hosts the Annual Brooks County History Fair, and in December it opens its doors for a festive Christmas Open House.
